{{Quote|I'm going to be sitting in a Z-95 cockpit wearing an EVA suit, and you want to sit on my lap? Worry less about being left behind and more about making certain the concussion missiles are fitted with the proper warheads, okay, buddy?|Poe Dameron, to BB-8|<ref name="Before the Awakening" />}}
The '''Z-95 Headhunter''', also referred to as the '''Z-95 starfighter''' or simply the '''Z-95''', was a multi-purpose [[starfighter]] jointly manufactured by [[Incom Corporation]] and [[Sublights Products Corporation]]. Despite being considered outdated, the Z-95 was durable and adaptable to a variety of different roles, which led many to recognize it as a versatile and respectable [[snub-fighter]] of its era. Countless variants of the Headhunter were produced, including one [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|model]] designed specifically for the [[Grand Army of the Republic]]'s [[Clone trooper pilot|clone pilots]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. The Z-95 was the forerunner of Incom's popular [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|I'm transmitting jump coordinates to your fighter. Ease out of the fight while Tarkin is concentrating on us. The Headhunter's hyperdrive will do the rest.|Salikk, to Berch Teller|<ref name="Tarkin" />}}
[[File:SWC_Z95.png|thumb|left|250px|A Z-95 Headhunter]]
Though already outdated<ref name="Clone Z-95 Starfighter" /> by the [[time]] it entered production,<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> the multi-purpose Z-95 Headhunter [[starfighter]] boasted endurance and adaptability and was largely recognized as a respectable and versatile [[snub-fighter]] of its era.<ref name="Clone Z-95 Starfighter" /> Named after the [[Coromon Headhunter]],<ref name="BMF 59">{{BuildFalconCite|59|Starship Fact File}}</ref> the Z-95 was equipped with two pairs of [[engine]]s,<ref name="Commander" /> the Z-95 was originally manufactured without a [[hyperdrive]], though it could be retrofitted with a rudimentary one.<ref name="Tarkin" /> However, as it lacked an [[astromech socket]], its [[pilot]] was forced to pre-program [[hyperspace route]]s or force-feed its [[Navigation computer|navicomputer]] jump coordinates provided by [[Datachip|data chips]]. The Z-95 was also noted for its cramped one-man [[cockpit]].<ref name="Before the Awakening" />

Despite these drawbacks, the Z-95 featured internal environmental controls<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> and a pair of wingtip-mounted,<ref name="Commander" /> high-powered [[blaster cannon]]s. It also boasted [[concussion missile launcher]]s<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> and a center-mounted [[ion cannon]], which was capable of penetrating [[deflector shield]]s.<ref name="Commander" /> The Z-95 was the forerunner of [[Incom Corporation|Incom's]] incredibly successful [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]], which implemented technologies and designs tested in the Z-95.<ref name="clone Z-95 starfighter" /> Another successor to the Headhunter was the [[Z-96]], introduced after the Clone Wars.<ref name="Bibo">{{Resistance|Bibo (episode)}}</ref>

==History==
===Prolific starfighter===
{{Quote|The Headhunter starfighters seen in the holovid could have come from anywhere.|An [[Unidentified Imperial technician (Sentinel Base)|Imperial technician]], following a rebel attack on Sentinel Base|<ref name="Tarkin" />}}
[[File:Clone_Z-95_starfighter_SWE.png|thumb|right|200px|The clone Z-95 starfighter, one of the Headhunter's countless variants]]
Jointly manufactured by Incom Corporation and [[Sublights Products Corporation|Subpro]],<ref name="clone Z-95 starfighter" /> the Z-95 Headhunter entered production during the [[Clone Wars]]<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> and spawned countless variants. The [[Galactic Republic]] made its own mark on the Headhunter's large production run with a [[Clone trooper pilot|clone-specific]] [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|model]].<ref name="Clone Z-95 Starfighter" /> [[Reaper Squadron]] was one unit that flew Headhunters. Decades after the end of the war, the wreckage of one of Reaper Squadron's Z-95s was recovered from [[Castilon]]'s [[Karavian Trench]] by [[Synara San]].<ref name="Bibo" /><ref name="Bucket's List">{{SW|url=news/buckets-list-extra-bibo-star-wars-resistance|text=Bucket's List Extra: 9 Fun Facts from "Bibo" - ''Star Wars Resistance''}}</ref>

Even after the war had ended, Z-95s were extremely common.<ref name="Tarkin" /> [[Idryssa Barruck]] flew a Headhunter during her time with [[Saw Gerrera]]'s [[Partisans]],<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> and several modified with basic hyperdrives and upgraded weaponry were used by [[Berch Teller]]'s [[Berch Teller's rebel cell|rebel cell]] in its [[Berch Teller campaign|fight]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. [[Hask Taff]], a member of Teller's cell, used several Headhunters to craft a false [[holovid]] that was transmitted to the Empire's [[Sentinel Base]]. The signal was meant to deceive the Imperials into believing that their [[Rampart Station]] had fallen under [[Attack on Sentinel Base|attack]], thus inciting them to protect the station and leave Sentinel Base vulnerable. However, [[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], the base's [[Commanding officer|commander]], detected that the message was a fraud and instead set a trap for the insurgents, who were immediately ambushed upon entering the [[Sentinel Base system|system]] and forced to retreat into [[hyperspace]]. The rebels later used Z-95s to [[Battle near the Gulf of Tatooine|attack]] an Imperial convoy near the [[Gulf of Tatooine]]; all but one were obliterated, as Teller used the remaining Headhunter to escape to the [[planet]] [[Christophsis]] while the rest of his cell was captured and summarily [[Death|executed]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> A gang of [[Pakiphantos]] also used Z-95s modified with [[proton cannon]]s. The gang tried to capture the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' on [[Dhandu 3]], but were outflown or outgunned.<ref name="Pirate's Price" />

===Venerable snub-fighter===
{{Quote|General, with respect, I've fought the First Order before and beat them every time. Once in a ship that had to be at least fifty years old.|Poe Dameron, to General Leia Organa, on fighting the First Order in a Z-95 Headhunter|<ref name="Poe Dameron 1">[[Poe Dameron 1|''Poe Dameron'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:Z-95_TCG_by_Chase_Toole.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Z-95 Headhunter taking off]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] continued to use Z-95s. Despite being slightly slower and less maneuverable than its successors, including the T-65B, the Z-95 proved a close-air-support staple of the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps]].<ref name="Commander" /> The [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|TIE fighter pilots]] of the [[Imperial Navy]] referred to Z-95s as "[[List of phrases and slang|skulls]]." During a [[Battle of Portocari|battle]] on [[Portocari]], Rebel Headhunters killed an Imperial pilot named [[Barsay]].<ref name="Last Call at the Zero Angle">{{InsiderCite|156|Last Call at the Zero Angle}}</ref>

Though they had long been retired from military use, Z-95s were a favorite among [[smuggler]]s, [[gangster]]s, [[pirate]]s, and a variety of others seeking to do both legitimate and illegitimate business<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> twenty-nine [[Standard year|years]] after the end of the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="Timeline">''[[Before the Awakening]]'' takes place shortly before [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], which ''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'' dates to twenty-nine [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Battle of Jakku]], the endpoint of the [[Galactic Civil War]].</ref> In one instance, [[Resistance]] [[Resistance pilot|pilot]] [[Poe Dameron]] acquired three Z-95s for a covert mission designated [[Operation: Sabre Strike]].<ref name="Before the Awakening" />

Pilots with the [[Citizens' Fleet]] flew Z-95s during the [[Battle of Exegol]] in<ref name="TROS Junior Novel">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]''</ref> [[35 ABY]].<ref name="TROS date">{{Film|IX}} events is dated to [[35 ABY]] as ''Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary'' states its events took place one [[Standard year|year]] after the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|Starkiller Incident]], which took place in [[34 BBY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''.</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Z-95 Headhunter made its first appearance in the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile game]] ''[[Star Wars: Commander]]'', published by [[Disney Interactive]]<ref name="Commander" /> on [[August 21]], [[2014]].<ref name="Star Wars: Commander release date">{{Tumblr|subdomain=disneyinteractive|url=post/97146518477/star-wars-commander-plans-have-been-intercepted|name=Disney Interactive|text="Star Wars: Commander" Plans Have Been Intercepted Detailing Who is Winning the Galactic Civil War|quote=Five million players have now joined the war (downloaded Star Wars: Commander since its launch on August 21).|archivefile=File:SWCommander-Tumblr.png}}</ref> Before that, it was referenced in the clone Z-95 starfighter entry in the now-discontinued [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]].<ref name="clone Z-95 starfighter" /> This entry, including the Z-95's mention, has since transferred over to the Encyclopedia's current replacement, the [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]].<ref name="Clone Z-95 Starfighter" /> The Z-95 Headhunter was originally created for the [[1979]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel ''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]'', written by [[Brian Daley]] as the first entry in [[Star Wars: The Han Solo Adventures|''The Han Solo Adventures'']] trilogy.<ref name="Han Solo at Stars' End">''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]''</ref>

While ''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]'' says the length of the Z-95 is 16.74 meters,<ref name="flightlog" /> ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]] [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 59|59]]'' says the ship is only 11.8 meters long.<ref name="BMF 59" /> This article assumes the former is correct.
